albums.title: Elis & Tom
albums.description:
One of the best MPB and bossa nova albums ever released, and the first track also happens to be my all time favorite. I have tried different versions of Águas de março (Waters of March), including Jobim's original ver, Sogumm and Chawool's cover, and Cibo Matto's, but Elis' rhythm and vocal are hard to beat.

A funny story from the production: a clash over modern instrumentation nearly caused a fiery 28-year-old Elis Regina to abandon the project in a rage. But the moment she and Tom Jobim began to play, the sheer magic of their musical chemistry melted away the hostility and forged a legendary collaboration.

albums.title: 淑樺的台灣歌
albums.description: I fell in love with the album cover first. This album is entirely in Hokkien, which I do not understand, but the production by one of my favorite artists, Jonathan Lee, alongside Japanese jazz artists Ken Shima and Asahi Jun, makes the lyrics almost beside the point. Just forget about the words and enjoy the synths, jazz fusion, and classic Taiwanese melodies.

albums.title: VESTA
albums.description: Recorded and produced in New York City, VESTA has a cosmopolitan skin and a Japanese soul. Eiko's voice feels born for this setting. The tracks are controlled, the instrumentation is smooth, and every part is choreographed to pair with the vocal. Everything is compacted into 30 minutes.

albums.title: Brasilian Skies
albums.description:
I knew Brazil has a big Japanese community, and this album popped up while I was searching for good MPB music. I listened through it assuming it was a Brazilian album.

Only after finishing (or not even fully finishing it) did I realize it was actually made by a Japanese artist who traveled to Rio de Janeiro to record it, blending samba and bossa nova with Japanese pop and synth. It’s just an absolutely amazing piece of work.

albums.title: Her Abiding Memory
albums.description:
I’m all for Shibuyakei albums, but most of them are fast paced, cosmopolitan, and ornamental. Think of works from Pizzicato Five or FPM. My Abiding Memory sits on the other end of that spectrum.

It was recorded on a budget, so the drum programming is simple, the acoustic guitars are crisp but unpolished, and the mix feels intimate. But the quality is no less amazing. It is more melodic, soft, and slow-paced.

I’ve been listening to it for over three months and still haven’t tired of it.

albums.title: Absolute Ego
albums.description: I realized I might have recommended too many Japanese albums, but this is yet another smooth and dreamy trip hop record. It is so good that I bought the entire album on iTunes just to get the two tracks missing from Apple Music. Please enjoy this one alone.

albums.title: Clube da Esquina

preview.trackTitle: Tudo o Que Você Podia Ser

albums.description:
2026 is only four months in, but I had not found many albums that really excited me, so I gave '70s MPB (Brazilian pop) a try.

When the guitar riff from 'Tudo o que voce podia ser' came in, I froze and listened all the way through; every second was pure enjoyment. This album is diverse and influential far beyond LATAM.

It is not the typical Brazilian bossa nova ocean breeze vibe you might think of. As the name suggests, the Corner Club feels like two friends making music for fun at their usual spot, casual, but still curated and controlled.

It also pushed me to explore more from Milton and Lo Borges.

albums.title: 卡拉OK.台北.我
albums.description: This album never had the greatest sales, but it is Tom Chang's most avant-garde work. It has aged like fine spirits, one sip pulls you straight to Taipei in the '90s, with everything so alive. No explanation is necessary, just hit play.

albums.title: Swing Swang Swung
albums.description:
Swing is such an understated duo. They are true legends of Chinese R&B. When you listen to the album all the way through, you will definitely wonder how they were making music like this back in the 2000s.

While the production and mixing may not sound as polished as modern studio albums, the lyrics, progressions, and melodies were far ahead of their time. As always, this is a compilation album, enjoy it from start to finish.

On a side note, Swing was originally called Snowman before they changed their name. If you find yourself wanting more, be sure to check out their earliest album under the name Snowman.

albums.title: Chasing Moving Trains
albums.description:
I liked blonded radio by Frank Ocean, not sure if it was discontinued, but it always had some interesting music. FANTAZIA was featured on blonded 10, and that led me to start listening to the Cat Heaven.

Then this album, Chasing Moving Trains, came out quietly in 2024, it was so quiet that I didn't discover it until a year later, lol.

But I'd been waiting for this pop-electronic sound from him for so long, and it really feels like a huge step forward from Cat Heaven.

I love the melodic lines and how the atmosphere evolves as you play through, finally peaking with the last song, 'Garden.' This is definitely a belated review, but I'm so glad to have this album with us.

albums.title: Smart?
albums.description: Tension was a Mandarin R&B band discovered by David Tao in LA. From start to end, it just feels as 20s Mandarin R&B as it gets, full of the good vibe and melody of the time I grew up with. This album was their debut, but it's equally complete and well-produced.

albums.title: Flying Beagle
albums.description:
This album played on my recommended radio while I was riding my bike, and I immediately pulled over to add it to my favorites. I’ve always liked Japanese fusion, and Flying Beagle is such a perfect example.

The instrumentation is so harmonious, and the piano flows so smoothly, it feels like driving down a newly paved asphalt road with no traffic. Hard to believe this came out 40 years ago.

albums.title: Go With The Flow
albums.description: Ayue hasn’t changed at all, he’s still the guy who truly enjoys life and turns those little details into melodies. This album is simply straightforward—sounds great and vibes great.

albums.title: HYPERYOUTH
albums.description: The perfect running pair, JVB’s music delivers the energy you need like a supercharged engine, making you want to dance and boosting your adrenaline. I fully enjoyed the retro, techno, and eclectic vibes from the start to the end.

albums.title: COБAKA (Crouka)
albums.description:
This album came out in 2001, but it feels way ahead of its time. The blend of synths, soundscapes, and jazzy instrumentation takes me back to the 70s and 80s, when imagination about outer space felt limitless.

Give this one a full listen and let it take you on a space journey. Apple Music’s recommendations are just getting better

albums.title: The Ocean Waves
albums.description:
Soundtracks from animes and games are amazing. Cowboy Bebop, K-On, and Sonny Boy, just to name a few are as good as the shows themselves. Ocean Waves is yet another excellent one.

The production is simple, capricious, but ahead of its time; you’d never guess it’s from 1993. The album feels narrative, enriched with synths that embody the 80s and 90s Japanese pop vibe. Hit the play button, cause this one will fix your busy brain.

albums.title: Forever Howlong
albums.description: Another red covered album - Forever Howlong is just a very surprising album out in 2025. I picked it up on my way to work, but starting from 'Besties,' its melodic yet baroque styled melody line and harmonic voicings kept me listening through and completely forgot about the crazy loud subway sound. And even setting aside BC,NR’s previous two albums, this one still holds up well on its own and is easy to enjoy independently.

albums.title: Sunlight
albums.description:
Herbie Hancock is a legendary and prolific jazz/fusion artist, and one of my personal favorites. He used to play the keys for the Miles Davis Quintet, and you might already know his iconic albums 'Head Hunters' and 'Maiden Voyage'.

But 'Sunlight' deserves just as much recognition. I Thought It Was You, features Herbie’s own vocals processed with a vocoder, adding a futuristic touch.

The album’s rhythms, basslines, and synth work were ahead of their time, influencing modern music works such as Daft Punk’s 'Random Access Memories'. The songs are around 8 minutes on average, but they're worth enjoying until the very last bit.

albums.title: Get Up
albums.description:
NewJeans is the first and only K-pop group I’ve really listened to. I’ve never had a K-pop album before because, to me, the culture seems to place a huge emphasis on music videos—like the music is meant to be enjopyed alongside the visuals. I am ignorant and don’t know much about Korean albums, but something about NewJeans feels different.

Their popular tracks like Ditto, ETA, and Hype Boy are simply great. They are short, sweet, with iconic Jersey club beats, garage vibes, and crystal-clear melodies. I can’t quite explain it, but these songs immediately take me back to my middle school Art Festival (藝術節) in 2012, just sitting with friends and watching people dance on stage. It just feels good listening to NewJeans with nothing in my head.

albums.title: You Will Never Know Why
albums.description:
You Will Never Know Why is a dreamy, upbeat album. With distant vocals and clear melody lines, it’s everything you’d expect from dream pop or synth pop. It literally takes me on a sweet trip, immersing myself in a beautifully crafted soundscape.

It’s been almost four years since my first listen, yet this album remains in my regular rotation. There are so many favorite tracks, like 'Acting', 'Darkness, 'Air Supply', and 'Pretending', to name a few.

albums.title: David Tao
albums.description:
David Tao’s self-titled debut album is, hands down, one of my favorite Chinese albums of all time. It’s the very definition of a perfect R&B album, it has beautiful vocals, melodies, and guitar, all in their purest form.

While David Tao has released several great albums like I’m OK and 黑色柳丁, this one stands out in how seamlessly it flows. From the moment Airport Takeoff starts playing, you’re fully immersed in his world.

Tracks like Blue Moon, Our Love, and Everything’s Gone are the holy grail of Chinese R&B—timeless, soulful, and flawless.

Every time I replay this album, I feel an overwhelming nostalgia for an era I never belonged to, back when music was made simply to sound good.

albums.title: Avantdale Bowling Club
albums.description:
This is the debut, self-titled jazz rap/hip-hop album by Avantdale Bowling Club (Tom Scott), a New Zealand-based artist. I never expected such a chill and quiet place like New Zealand to produce a hip-hop album this good.

The composition is clean yet capricious, and the production has a smooth, rhythm-rich feel, much like the works by D'Angelo and Kendrick.

Songs like 'Years Gone By' and 'Old Dogs' feel like listening to a jazz quartet with a storyteller at the mic, while 'F(R)Iends' leans more toward a full jazz orchestra in the background. Overall, it’s a very good album, best enjoyed from start to finish.

albums.title: 加爾基 精液 栗ノ花
albums.description:
Without a doubt, this is the best work from Sheena Ringo (椎名林檎). Compared to her previous two albums ('Winning Strip' and 'Innocence Moratorium'), this one is far more diverse and playful. From the moment the first song ('Religion') starts, I get goosebumps, it’s that good. 

In this album, Sheena masters the dynamics of an album, striking a perfect balance between serenity and chaos, simplicity and complexity. She also blends traditional Japanese melodies and instruments with modern production and composition, perfectly demonstrated in 'Stem' and 'Rush Job'. I don’t want to say too much because this album speaks for itself — freedom within order.

albums.title: Freak Smile
albums.description:
One of the best shibuya-kei (渋谷系) albums from the 90s. Unfortunately, it's not available on most music streaming platforms.

The album expertly blends Japanese Jazz Fusion, orchestral elements, electronics, R&B, and even touches of new age and experimental sounds, carefully layered together.

It somehow reminds me of Sheena Ringo's 'Kalk Samen Chesnut Flower' - sharing the same level of richness and complexity, but choreographed in a beautiful way.

albums.title: Beta
albums.description:
I stumbled upon this album while casually browsing Rate Your Music, but it really clicked with me on my second listen, a couple of months after the first. It’s a rich, indie, and playful album, blending R&B chords with deep synth bass.

Lots of surprises when I played it all the way through. It is similar to some of Honne’s early songs, just good vibes and great melodies. My favorite tracks are People Never Change, 21C, Black and White, and Control Room.
